03 Component reverse index

Bangla name: কম্পোনেন্ট রিভার্স ইনডেক্স

← Contents · Traceability matrix

The matrix (02) goes feature → component. This page goes the other way: component → feature. Use it when you have a table, a queue, a Redis key, a worker or an endpoint and need to know what depends on it — before you rename it, drop it, or change its shape.

1. How to use this page

You are about to… Look at
Change a table's columns §3 — who else maps it
Rename a Redis key §4 — who reads it
Change a queue's message shape §5 — who produces and consumes it
Delete a controller 91 · Endpoint index, then §2
Delete a worker §6

Anything marked shared has more than one service mapping it. Those are the changes that break something quietly.

3.5 The shared-table problem

These tables are mapped by more than one service with ExcludeFromMigrations, so no single service owns their schema:

Discounts · DiscountAssigns · DiscountAssignEvent · DiscountAssignVenueGallery
VenueGalleries · GalleryBlocks · BlockLevels · EventVenueDetails
PromoCodes · PromoCodeAssigns · EventPromoCodeAssign · PromoCodeAssignVenueGallery
Currencies · Events · PromoCodeVenueEventGallery
TicketLayoutConfigs · BookedUserRecords · ProgramTeams · Venues · EventSegments · EventSettings
TicketCheckerGates · TicketCheckerGateUsers · BlockLevelEntryGates
UserBookingOrders

Consequence. A column rename in Admin will not fail the build in Booking or Ticketing — the mappings are read-only views, so the break appears at runtime as a missing column. This is the single largest schema-change hazard in the platform, and it depends on the unresolved database-layout question (Q-02).

See X-19, S-17 and X-24.

5. Queue reverse index

Queue Message shape Producer Consumer Feature
OrderSuccess booking order id Booking Ticketing TicketGenerationService S-07
EventCapacity capacity event Booking Booking LevelCapacityUpdateService, EventLiveCapacityUpdateService S-01, S-02
VatChallanProcessing order id Booking Scheduler VatChallanProcessingService S-10
TicketSigning TicketSigningPayload Ticketing Ticketing S-08
TicketProcessing TicketProcessingRequest { ReservationId, ProcessingType = Merge\|Zip, GroupId, OrderId } Ticketing Utility TicketProcessingService S-09
FirebaseNotification FirebaseNotificationRequest { Title, Body, Data, DeviceTokens, CreatedAt, GroupId, OrderId } PushNotification Scheduler FirebaseNotificationService S-11

Before changing any message shape, read Q-09: there is no dead-letter queue and the retry counter never advances, so a shape mismatch retries for ever rather than failing visibly.

The files a newcomer is most likely to need, by role.

7.1 Backend entry points

What Where

7.2 Per-service structure

Each service follows the same split:

Layer What lives there
ETP.<Name>.Service/Api/ Controllers — thin, delegate to managers
ETP.<Name>.Domain/Managers/ The business logic. This is where to read
ETP.<Name>.Storage/DbContexts/ DbContext, DbSets, ExcludeFromMigrations
ETP.<Name>.Storage/Migrations/ Migrations — only for tables the service owns
ETP.<Name>.Client/ Typed HTTP client other services use
ETP.<Name>.Integration/ External system clients (TSP, DgePay, OneID, SES)
